subject: dogs
one_liner: Five-minute language lessons for dogs, built around a streak your dog will not remember having.
brand_voice_notes: Consumer edtech cheer delivered by a growth team that has read every retention memo and none of the veterinary literature. Treats a dog's six-word vocabulary as a serious addressable market. The mascot is Gerald, a squirrel, who handles all push notifications and has no boundaries. Never admits dogs cannot read the app. Numbers are precise and small.

hero.h1: Your dog knows four words. We can get that to six.
hero.sub: Stay is the language app for dogs. Five-minute lessons, a daily streak your dog will not remember, and Gerald, a squirrel who sends a reminder every nine seconds.

features.title: Streaks sized for a nine-second memory
features.blurb: Most apps remind you once a day. Your dog forgets the reminder before it finishes. Gerald re-sends it every nine seconds, around the clock, from the window ledge.

features.title: One word, five languages
features.blurb: Your household has been spelling out W-A-L-K for years. Stay teaches 'walk' in Spanish, French, Portuguese, Korean and Pig Latin, so there is nowhere left to hide.

features.title: Leaderboards by fire hydrant
features.blurb: Your dog is ranked against every dog who has visited the same hydrant this week. Rankings refresh on contact. The top dog is a beagle called Doug and nobody knows how.

demo_screen_concept: A Stay lesson screen on a phone-width layout. Top bar: a 41-day streak flame, five bone-shaped health icons, and an XP bar. The prompt card asks the dog to translate a phrase like '¿Quién es un buen chico?' and offers four chunky answer tiles that are dog actions (Sit, Tilt head, Bark once, Roll over). Picking an answer lips the tile down, then a CHECK button slides up a green 'Correct!' or red 'Not quite' bottom sheet; wrong answers cost a bone. Gerald the squirrel sits in a speech bubble on the side with rotating guilt messages. A tab bar switches to a hydrant leaderboard (Doug the beagle on top, your dog in 14th) and a 'words learned' list of six words with per-language toggles.

design_direction.style: Flat gamified mobile-edtech, cobalt daylight mode. A chunky, cheerful language-learning app rendered fully flat: solid fills, thick rounded shapes, and buttons with a hard darker bottom lip that presses down on click, like a toy. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: clay shadow stacks, silk threads, leg meters, exuvia outlines, washi paper, wall labels, empty plinths, LCD greens, parts diagrams, warning boxes, rhumb lines, cartouches, wax seals, acorn marks, dot maps, terminal panels, name tags, punch cards, thermal tickets, matte dark mode, lime LEDs. Also absent: dark backgrounds, glassmorphism, gradients, blurred drop shadows, serif type, paper textures. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The lip button: every button and answer tile has a 4px solid bottom border one shade darker, and translates down 4px on press. (2) The lesson path: features and pricing tiers sit on a zig-zag column of round lesson nodes joined by a dotted trail, like a skill tree. (3) The bone meter: health and tier strength shown as rows of small flat bone glyphs. (4) Gerald: a flat squirrel mascot in an orange speech bubble that delivers all the guilt. Squeaky-toy orange #FF7A2F is rationed to Gerald, the streak flame and the highlighted tier. Corners 16px on cards, 14px on buttons. No shadows except the bottom lips.
design_direction.archetype: App-store style consumer app landing: hero with phone mockup, feature path, reviews, pricing, download CTA
design_direction.motion_vocab: Press-down lips (translateY 4px, 80ms), a bouncy pop on correct answers (scale 1 to 1.08 to 1, 220ms), the streak flame flickering via a 2-frame scale loop, XP bar filling with ease-out. All motion disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns on desktop. Left: small cobalt pill 'Now with 6 words', the h1 in heavy Fredoka at 64px, sub, a lipped cobalt CTA plus a white lipped secondary 'open the demo'. Right: a hero photo of a dog in a flat cobalt-backed frame with a floating lipped streak card ('41-day streak') and Gerald's orange speech bubble overlapping the corner. Stacks on mobile with the photo first.
